Look at the confusion matrix before any single summary number.

cards.title: Precisão
cards.text: De tudo o que o modelo assinalou, quanto estava certo? Uma precisão alta significa poucos falsos alarmes.

deep.x: Precision answers: when the model raises an alert, how often is it right? It matters when false alarms are expensive or erode trust.
When precision matters most

items.b: too many false alarms get ignored

deep.x: Alert fatigue
Security and monitoring teams faced with mostly false alarms start ignoring alerts, including real ones. Raising precision can make a system more useful even if it catches slightly less.
In medical screening, precision is called positive predictive value: for rare diseases, even accurate tests can produce more false positives than true ones.

cards.title: Sensibilidade (recall)
cards.text: De todos os casos reais, quantos é que o modelo apanhou? Uma sensibilidade alta significa poucas falhas.

deep.x: Recall, also called sensitivity, answers: of all the real cases, how many did we catch? It matters when misses are dangerous or costly.
When recall matters most

items.b: a missed fault can cause accidents
missing a sanctioned party is illegal

deep.x: Two-stage systems
A common design uses a high-recall first stage to catch almost everything, then a high-precision second stage (another model or humans) to filter false alarms.

steps: Stage 2: precise model or human review

deep.x: Specificity
The counterpart for negatives is specificity: of all genuine negatives, how many were correctly cleared? Medical tests usually report sensitivity and specificity together.
Recall without precision floods teams with work; precision without recall misses the problem. You need both in balance.

cards.title: O compromisso entre precisão e sensibilidade
cards.text: Baixa o limiar de alarme e apanhas mais (a sensibilidade sobe), mas lanças mais falsos alarmes (a precisão desce). Sobe-o e acontece o contrário. Onde o pôr é uma escolha de negócio.

deep.x: Most classifiers output a score; you choose a threshold. Moving it trades precision for recall. Plotting the two across thresholds gives a precision–recall curve.
Choosing the threshold
Pick the threshold that minimises expected cost or meets a constraint ("catch at least 90% of fraud" or "no more than 50 alerts a day for the team").
Capacity matters
If a compliance team can review 200 cases a day, the threshold should produce about 200 alerts, ranked by score, regardless of the abstract "best" F1.
ROC curves
ROC curves plot recall against the false-positive rate. For very imbalanced data, precision–recall curves are usually more informative.
The threshold is a business decision, not a technical one; data scientists should present the options, and owners should choose.

cards.title: Pontuação F1
cards.text: A F1 combina precisão e sensibilidade num único número, a sua média harmónica. Só é alta quando ambas são altas.

deep.x: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. Unlike a simple average, it's dragged down by whichever is lower, so a model can't score well by excelling at one and failing at the other.
Harmonic vs simple average
Variants
Limits
F1 ignores true negatives and treats both error types as equally bad. If false negatives cost 100 times more than false positives, a cost-based metric is better.
F1 is a handy summary for comparing models, but business decisions need costs.

cards.title: Erros para números
cards.text: Na regressão, mede-se a que distância as previsões ficam da realidade. O MAE é o erro absoluto médio ("falha em média 8000 €"). O RMSE castiga mais os erros grandes. O MAPE dá o erro em percentagem.

deep.x: Regression and forecasting use error metrics measured in the target's units or percentages.

items.b: average absolute error, easy to explain
average signed error, systematic over- or under-prediction

deep.x: Example
Actual sales: 100, 120, 80. Forecasts: 110, 100, 90. Errors: 10, −20, 10.
MAPE's trap
MAPE explodes when actual values are near zero (selling 1 unit vs forecasting 3 is a 200% error). Weighted MAPE (WAPE) or MAE are often more robust for intermittent demand.
Bias matters
A forecast can have low average error but systematically under-predict, causing chronic stock-outs. Track bias separately.
In supply chains, forecast accuracy is often reported as 1 − WAPE, e.g. "85% forecast accuracy".

cards.title: Compara com uma referência
cards.text: Uma previsão com 10% de erro parece boa até descobrires que "igual à semana passada" dá 11%. Apresenta sempre o teu modelo ao lado de uma referência simples e do processo humano atual.

deep.x: A metric only has meaning in comparison. The relevant comparisons are a naive baseline, the current process and the cost of being wrong.
Forecast value added
Supply-chain teams measure "forecast value added": how much each step (statistical model, planner adjustments) improves on the naive forecast. Sometimes manual adjustments make forecasts worse.
Statistical significance
Small improvements may be noise. Test on enough data, across time periods, and check confidence intervals before claiming a win.
If you can't beat "same as last week", don't deploy a complex model.

cards.title: Testa como vai ser usado
cards.text: Avalia com dados que se pareçam com o futuro: datas posteriores, clientes novos, outras regiões. Depois continua a monitorizar após o lançamento, porque o verdadeiro teste começa no primeiro dia em produção.

deep.x: Offline test scores often overestimate real performance. A good evaluation mimics production: same data sources, same timing, same population.

items: Hold out the most recent period
Test on new customers and regions

deep.x: Shadow mode and A/B tests
In shadow mode, the model makes predictions alongside the existing process without acting on them, so you compare safely. A/B tests then expose part of real traffic to the new model.
Monitoring in production
Many teams discover data pipeline bugs only in shadow mode, when production inputs turn out to be formatted differently from the training data.

cards.title: Mede o que importa para o negócio
cards.text: Um modelo 2% mais preciso mas que demora 10 segundos por previsão, ou que não pode ser explicado a um regulador, pode ser pior. Traduz os erros em dinheiro, tempo ou risco.

deep.x: Technical metrics are proxies. Decision-makers care about revenue, cost, risk, customer experience and compliance.
Example

Raising a churn model's recall from 60% to 70% might identify 1,000 more at-risk customers a year. If retention offers save 20% of them at a margin of €300 each, that's about €60,000 a year, minus offer costs.

x: 1,000 extra customers × 20% saved
= 200 customers
× €300 margin = €60,000 a year

deep.x: Non-functional requirements

x: Latency: card payments need decisions in milliseconds
Cost per prediction, especially with large language models
Robustness, fairness and auditability

deep.x: Present model results in the language of the business owner, not the data scientist.

quiz.q: Há 50 casos reais de fraude; o modelo apanha 40. A sensibilidade (recall) é…
quiz.explain: Sensibilidade = 40 ÷ 50 = 80%.

quiz.q: Que métrica responde a "dos alertas lançados, quantos eram reais?"
quiz.explain: A precisão mede até que ponto os alertas são fiáveis.

quiz.q: Porque é que 99% de exatidão pode ser enganador?
options: Quando a classe positiva é rara, dizer sempre 'não' dá uma pontuação alta
A exatidão só funciona com imagens
quiz.explain: Com 1% de fraude, um modelo que não faz nada tem 99% de exatidão.

lessons.title: Visão computacional
lessons.summary: Como as máquinas veem: píxeis, convoluções e deteção de objetos.

cards.title: Uma imagem é uma grelha de números
cards.text: Para um computador, uma foto é uma grelha de píxeis, cada um guardado como três números para o vermelho, o verde e o azul, de 0 a 255. Uma foto de telemóvel de 12 megapíxeis tem cerca de 36 milhões de números.

deep.x: A colour image is stored as three grids (channels) of brightness values, one each for red, green and blue. Each value typically ranges from 0 to 255 (8 bits).
Preprocessing
Vision models usually resize images to a fixed size (e.g. 224×224 or 512×512) and normalise values to small ranges. Higher resolution improves detail but costs more compute.
Beyond RGB

x: Thermal cameras: temperature per pixel
Depth cameras: distance per pixel
Satellite imagery: dozens of spectral bands beyond visible light
Medical scans: 3D volumes, like CT slices

deep.x: A 4K video at 30 frames per second produces about 750 million pixel values every second.

cards.title: Classificação
cards.text: A tarefa de visão mais simples: o que há nesta imagem? A rede devolve uma probabilidade para cada categoria que conhece.

deep.x: Image classification assigns one or more labels to a whole image. The network's last layer produces a score per class; softmax converts scores to probabilities that sum to 100%.
Top-1 and top-5
ImageNet results are reported as top-1 accuracy (correct class is the top guess) and top-5 (correct class in the top five). Modern models exceed 90% top-1.
Business uses
Open-vocabulary models
Models like CLIP (2021) learn from image–caption pairs, so you can classify into new categories just by describing them in words, without retraining.
Classification says what's in the picture, not where; detection and segmentation add location.

cards.title: Deteção de objetos
cards.text: A deteção vai mais longe: encontra cada objeto e desenha uma caixa à volta de cada um, com uma etiqueta e uma pontuação de confiança. É o que sistemas de câmaras de vigilância como o Frigate usam para distinguir uma pessoa de um carro que passa ou de um gato.

deep.x: Object detection outputs a set of bounding boxes, each with a class label and confidence. Detectors must handle many objects of different sizes, partially hidden or overlapping.
Popular models
Confidence thresholds
Each box has a confidence. Home camera systems like Frigate let you set minimum scores per object type, and "zones" so that only a person in the driveway triggers an alert.
Measuring detectors
Detection is scored with mean Average Precision (mAP), based on how well predicted boxes overlap true boxes (intersection over union, IoU).
YOLO-style models can run at dozens of frames per second on small accelerators like a Google Coral or a phone chip.

cards.title: Segmentação
cards.text: A segmentação etiqueta cada píxel: estrada, carro, peão, céu. Os carros autónomos e a imagiologia médica dependem dela para conhecer as formas exatas e não apenas caixas.

deep.x: Segmentation classifies every pixel. It gives exact outlines, essential when shape and area matter.

items: Semantic: every pixel gets a class

deep.x: Uses
Segment Anything
Meta's Segment Anything Model (2023) can cut out almost any object from a click or box prompt, trained on over 1 billion masks. It made segmentation a general-purpose tool.
Area measurements
Because segmentation gives pixel-exact shapes, you can measure things: the burnt area of a forest from satellite images, the size of a lesion, or the coverage of rust on a ship.
Choose the simplest output that serves the decision: a label, a box or a mask.

cards.title: O ImageNet mudou tudo
cards.text: O ImageNet é um conjunto de dados com mais de 14 milhões de imagens etiquetadas. Em 2012, uma rede profunda chamada AlexNet ganhou a sua competição anual por uma margem enorme, reduzindo a taxa de erro de cerca de 26% para 15%. Esse resultado deu início ao boom da aprendizagem profunda.

deep.x: ImageNet, led by Fei-Fei Li and launched in 2009, organised over 14 million images into about 22,000 categories, labelled by crowd workers. Its annual challenge (ILSVRC) used a 1,000-category subset.
Why AlexNet mattered
AlexNet, by Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever and Geoffrey Hinton, combined deep CNNs, ReLU, dropout and GPU training. The jump convinced the field to switch to deep learning almost overnight.
Lessons

x: Big, well-labelled benchmarks drive progress
But benchmarks can be "overfit" by the community
ImageNet also revealed problematic labels and biases, prompting dataset audits

deep.x: The human error rate on ImageNet's top-5 task was estimated at about 5%, by researcher Andrej Karpathy, who labelled images himself.

cards.title: Aprendizagem por transferência

steps: Modelo treinado com milhões de imagens

cards.text: Raramente se treina um modelo de visão de raiz. Pega-se num já treinado com milhões de imagens e afina-se com umas centenas das tuas, como fotos de peças com defeito.

deep.x: Transfer learning reuses knowledge from a large pre-trained model. You keep the general feature-extracting layers and retrain only the last layers, or fine-tune everything gently, on your smaller dataset.

steps: Add new layer for your classes

deep.x: How much data?
Options

items.b: freeze the backbone, train the head
describe classes in text, no training

deep.x: Industrial example
A factory with 300 photos of good parts and 200 of defective ones can fine-tune a pre-trained model to spot defects with high accuracy in hours, not months.
The same principle powers language models: pre-train once at huge cost, then adapt cheaply to many tasks.

cards.title: Reconhecimento ótico de caracteres
cards.text: O OCR transforma imagens de texto em texto: faturas digitalizadas, matrículas, placas. O OCR moderno também percebe a disposição, por isso sabe que número é o total e qual é a data.

deep.x: OCR began with matching letter templates; modern OCR uses deep learning to read printed and handwritten text in many languages and layouts.
Document AI
Invoice and contract processing combines OCR with layout understanding and language models: "Total" next to "€1,250.00" becomes a structured field, even if every supplier's invoice looks different.
Vision-language models
Recent multimodal LLMs can read a document image directly and answer questions about it, often replacing separate OCR and extraction pipelines.
Accuracy matters
A misread digit in a price or quantity can be costly. Production systems add validation rules, confidence thresholds and human review for low-confidence fields.
In commodity trading and logistics, extracting data from contracts, bills of lading and certificates is a high-value AI use case.

cards.title: Visão na periferia (edge)
cards.text: Muitas câmaras correm agora a deteção localmente em pequenos aceleradores, em vez de enviarem o vídeo para a nuvem. É mais rápido, mais barato e mantém as imagens privadas.

deep.x: Edge AI runs models on local devices: cameras, phones, gateways, cars. Specialised low-power accelerators, like NPUs and Google Coral TPUs, make real-time detection possible on a few watts.
Making models small

items.b: small model learns from a big one

deep.x: Home example
A home NVR like Frigate decodes camera streams and runs object detection locally, only recording and alerting on people or cars, with no video sent to the cloud.
A Coral USB accelerator performs around 4 trillion operations per second using about 2 watts.

cards.title: Quando a visão falha
cards.text:
Os modelos de visão podem ser enganados por iluminação invulgar, ângulos estranhos, chuva na lente ou objetos que nunca viram no treino. Um modelo treinado no verão pode ter dificuldades com neve.

Testa nas condições reais em que a câmara vai estar.

deep.x: Vision models learn from training images; anything outside that range is risky. Failures can be subtle and surprising.
Shortcut learning
Models sometimes learn spurious cues. A famous example: a model distinguishing wolves from huskies relied on snow in the background, not the animals.

deep.r: It may be recognising background clues that happened to correlate

deep.x: Adversarial examples
Tiny, carefully designed changes to an image, invisible to people, can make a model misclassify it. Stickers on stop signs have fooled sign recognisers in experiments.
Robustness practices

items: Test by condition: night, rain, angle
Keep humans in the loop for critical uses

deep.x: Deploy vision where you've tested it, and expect surprises where you haven't.

cards.title: Os rostos são especiais
cards.text: O reconhecimento facial identifica pessoas concretas e é juridicamente sensível. Ao abrigo do Regulamento da IA da UE, a identificação biométrica remota em tempo real em espaços públicos pela polícia é proibida, exceto em casos restritos e autorizados.

deep.x: Face recognition compares a face's numerical "faceprint" against a database. It's biometric data, a special category under GDPR, and its use is tightly restricted.
Under the EU AI Act

x: Untargeted scraping of facial images to build databases is prohibited
Emotion recognition in workplaces and schools is prohibited, with narrow exceptions
Real-time remote biometric identification by police in public is banned except in narrowly defined, authorised cases
Other biometric systems are classed as high-risk

deep.x: Accuracy and bias
Top algorithms are extremely accurate in ideal conditions, but error rates vary by image quality and demographic group. Wrongful arrests based on faulty matches have been documented in the USA.
Your phone's face unlock stores a mathematical template on the device, not your photo, and doesn't send it to the cloud.

quiz.q: Desenhar caixas etiquetadas à volta de cada pessoa e carro numa imagem é…
quiz.explain: A deteção localiza cada objeto com uma caixa.

quiz.q: Afinar um modelo pré-treinado com milhões de imagens usando umas centenas de fotos tuas chama-se…
quiz.explain: Transferes o que ele já aprendeu para a tua tarefa.

quiz.q: O que aconteceu com a AlexNet em 2012?
options: Ganhou o ImageNet por larga margem e desencadeou o boom da aprendizagem profunda
quiz.explain: O seu erro foi muito inferior ao dos métodos anteriores.

lessons.title: Fala e som
lessons.summary: Como as máquinas ouvem, transcrevem e respondem em voz.

cards.title: O som como imagem
cards.text: O áudio é uma onda de pressão do ar, amostrada milhares de vezes por segundo. Os modelos de IA costumam convertê-lo num espetrograma: uma imagem de que frequências soam alto em cada momento. Depois podem aplicar-se técnicas do mundo das imagens.

deep.x: Sound is a pressure wave. A microphone measures it thousands of times per second. A spectrogram shows, for each short time slice, how much energy each frequency has, turning sound into an image.
Mel spectrograms
Human hearing is more sensitive to differences in low frequencies. Mel spectrograms space frequencies the way we perceive them, and are the standard input for speech models.
Reading a spectrogram
Vowels show bands of energy called formants; "s" sounds appear as high-frequency noise; silence is dark. Trained phoneticians can partly "read" speech from spectrograms.
Some modern models skip spectrograms and learn directly from raw waveforms, but spectrograms remain common.

cards.title: Taxas de amostragem
cards.text: As chamadas telefónicas são normalmente amostradas 8000 vezes por segundo, o que chega para a fala. Os CD usam 44 100, o suficiente para captar tudo o que os humanos conseguem ouvir (até cerca de 20 kHz).

deep.x: By the Nyquist–Shannon theorem, to capture a frequency you must sample at least twice that rate. Human hearing tops out around 20 kHz, so 44.1 kHz captures it all.
Bit depth
Each sample also has a precision: 16 bits gives 65,536 levels (CD), 24 bits for studio work. Higher bit depth means a wider dynamic range between quiet and loud.
Speech models
Most speech recognition models use 16 kHz audio: enough for intelligibility while keeping data small.
Higher sampling rates mostly matter for music and audio production, not speech AI.

cards.title: Da fala ao texto
cards.text:
O reconhecimento automático de fala (ASR) transforma fala em palavras. Os sistemas modernos são treinados com centenas de milhares de horas de áudio e lidam com sotaques, ruído e várias línguas.

O modelo aberto Whisper, da OpenAI, lançado em 2022, foi treinado com 680 000 horas.

deep.x: Modern automatic speech recognition (ASR) uses end-to-end neural networks: audio in, text out. Transformer-based models like Whisper learn from huge, diverse datasets, making them robust to accents, noise and technical vocabulary.
Measuring accuracy
ASR is scored by word error rate (WER): substitutions, deletions and insertions divided by the number of words. Clean English can be under 5%; noisy calls or rare languages are higher.
Practical tips

x: Custom vocabularies help with names and jargon
Speaker microphones matter more than model tweaks
Portuguese from Portugal and Brazil differ; check models handle European Portuguese well

deep.x: Whisper was trained on 680,000 hours of audio, roughly 77 years of continuous listening.

cards.title: Do texto à fala
cards.text: O TTS funciona ao contrário. As vozes neuronais já soam naturais, com respiração e ênfase. Algumas conseguem clonar uma voz a partir de uma amostra curta, o que levanta preocupações de fraude.

deep.x: Modern TTS generates natural speech in two stages: a model predicts acoustic features (often a mel spectrogram) from text, and a vocoder turns them into a waveform. Newer models generate audio tokens directly.
Natural voices
Uses

x: Accessibility: screen readers for blind and low-vision users
Audiobooks and dubbing
Customer service voices
Reading apps, like the Listen button in this one

deep.x: Voice cloning risks
Cloning a voice from a short sample enables fraud and impersonation. Responsible providers require consent and add watermarks; the EU AI Act requires disclosure of AI-generated audio deepfakes.
People who lose their voice to illnesses like ALS can now "bank" their voice beforehand and speak with a synthetic version of it.

cards.title: Assistentes de voz: uma cadeia
cards.text: Um assistente de voz encadeia vários modelos: um pequeno fica à escuta da palavra de ativação, o ASR transcreve o pedido, um modelo de linguagem percebe a intenção e o TTS diz a resposta.

deep.x: Classic voice assistants chain specialised components. Each step can fail, and errors compound.
Newer: end-to-end voice models
Recent "speech-to-speech" models handle listening, reasoning and speaking in one model, reducing delay and preserving tone and emotion, allowing natural interruptions.
Latency budget
Natural conversation needs responses within about 300–500 ms. Each pipeline stage adds delay, so engineers optimise every step.
Home automation
Local voice assistants, like those in Home Assistant, run wake words and recognition on local hardware, keeping commands private.
The hardest part isn't hearing words; it's understanding intent in messy, real conversations.

cards.title: As palavras de ativação correm localmente
cards.text: O teu telemóvel ou coluna inteligente não está a enviar tudo para a nuvem. Um modelo minúsculo no aparelho só está à escuta de "Hey…". Só depois de este disparar é que o áudio sai do aparelho.

deep.x: A wake-word model is tiny (often under 1 MB) and runs continuously on a low-power chip, listening only for one phrase. It keeps a short rolling buffer of audio, discarded unless the wake word is detected.

steps: Tiny model checks for wake word
If detected: stream to main recognition

deep.x: Trade-offs
Privacy realities
False wake-ups do happen, sending snippets to the cloud. In 2019, reports revealed contractors at several tech companies reviewed some recordings to improve accuracy, prompting changes and opt-outs.
Some open-source projects let you train your own custom wake word with a few minutes of synthetic samples.

cards.title: Diarização de oradores
cards.text: Numa gravação de reunião, a diarização responde a "quem falou quando?". Combinada com a transcrição, produz atas com nomes associados.

deep.x: Diarisation segments audio by speaker. It uses voice embeddings, numerical voiceprints, and clusters segments that sound like the same person.
Challenges
Meeting assistants
Meeting tools combine diarisation, transcription and language models to produce summaries, action items and who-said-what.
Consent
Recording and transcribing meetings involves personal data; inform participants and follow company policies and local law.
Diarisation says who spoke when; speaker identification says which named person it was, which requires enrolment.

cards.title: Para além da fala
cards.text: A IA de áudio também reconhece outros sons: um vidro a partir-se, um bebé a chorar, um rolamento de uma máquina a começar a falhar. A manutenção preditiva muitas vezes está à escuta de alterações na vibração e no ruído.

deep.x: Audio AI classifies all kinds of sounds. Models trained on large sound datasets, like Google's AudioSet with over 2 million clips, recognise hundreds of sound types.
Predictive maintenance
Bearings, pumps and motors change their sound and vibration as they wear. Acoustic and vibration sensors with anomaly detection can warn weeks before failure.
Nature monitoring
Recorders in forests identify bird and frog species by their calls, and can detect chainsaws for anti-logging efforts. BirdNET identifies thousands of bird species from audio.
Some hospitals trial AI that listens to coughs or breathing sounds as a screening aid.

cards.title: Vozes deepfake

items.r: ligar de volta para um número conhecido
verificar cada pedido de pagamento invulgar

cards.text:
Com alguns segundos da voz de alguém, as ferramentas modernas conseguem criar áudio falso convincente. Há burlões que usaram vozes clonadas de administradores para pedir pagamentos urgentes.

Combina passos de verificação para qualquer pedido de pagamento invulgar, seja qual for a voz.

deep.x: Voice cloning needs only seconds of audio, easily taken from videos, calls or voicemail. Scams have used cloned voices of executives, and of family members in distress, to request urgent payments.
Notable cases

In 2019 a UK energy firm's CEO was reportedly tricked into transferring about €220,000 after a call mimicking his boss's voice. In 2024 a Hong Kong employee paid out about US$25 million after a video call with deepfaked colleagues.
Defences

items: Call back on a known number
Use code words for urgent requests

deep.w: If it sounds like them, it is them
deep.r: Voice and even video can now be convincingly faked

deep.x: Detection
Detection tools exist but are an arms race. Process controls (verification and approval rules) are more reliable than trying to spot fakes by ear.
Trust the process, not the voice.

cards.title: Tradução por voz
cards.text: Junta reconhecimento de fala, tradução automática e síntese de fala e obténs tradução falada quase em tempo real. Alguns sistemas já traduzem a fala diretamente, sem escrever texto pelo meio.

deep.x: Spoken translation combines speech recognition, machine translation and speech synthesis, or does it all in one model. Latency and accuracy have improved rapidly.
Direct speech-to-speech
Newer models translate speech without writing intermediate text, preserving the speaker's tone and even voice. Meta's SeamlessM4T and similar models support dozens of languages.
Limits

x: Idioms, humour and cultural references
Specialist terminology without context
Names and numbers misheard
Simultaneous interpretation of fast speech

deep.x: Earbuds now offer near real-time translation of conversations, an idea straight out of science fiction's "Babel fish".

quiz.q: O que é um espetrograma?
options: Uma imagem de que frequências soam alto ao longo do tempo
quiz.explain: Transforma o áudio numa grelha parecida com uma imagem.

quiz.q: Porque é que as colunas inteligentes detetam a palavra de ativação no próprio aparelho?
options: É rápido, barato e mantém privado o áudio do dia a dia
A nuvem não percebe palavras de ativação
quiz.explain: Só depois da palavra de ativação é que o áudio é enviado.

quiz.q: Qual é a resposta mais segura a um pedido de pagamento urgente com a voz de um chefe?
options: Confirmar por um canal separado e conhecido
quiz.explain: As vozes podem ser clonadas; a confirmação não pode depender da própria chamada.

lessons.title: Sistemas de recomendação
lessons.summary: Como a Netflix, a Amazon e o Spotify decidem o que te mostrar.

cards.title: O problema da recomendação

steps: Reduzir a umas centenas de candidatos

cards.text: Uma loja pode ter um milhão de produtos; tu vais olhar para umas dezenas. Os sistemas de recomendação preveem quais desses poucos é mais provável quereres, a partir do teu histórico e do de pessoas parecidas contigo.

deep.x: Recommenders rank a huge catalogue for each user. Large platforms usually work in stages to handle millions of items fast.
Signals used
Objectives
Recommenders optimise something measurable: clicks, purchases, watch time, retention. Choosing the objective shapes behaviour: optimising clicks alone can promote sensational content.
Amazon's item-to-item collaborative filtering, described in 2003, became one of the most influential recommender designs.

cards.title: Filtragem colaborativa

items: gostaram de A, B, C e D

cards.text: "Quem comprou isto também comprou…" O sistema encontra utilizadores com gostos semelhantes aos teus e recomenda aquilo de que eles gostaram. Não precisa de perceber nada dos próprios produtos.

deep.x: Collaborative filtering uses the pattern of interactions across all users. If you and another user liked many of the same items, items they liked that you haven't seen are good candidates.

items: find items liked by the same users

deep.x: Matrix factorisation
Think of a giant table of users × items, mostly empty. Matrix factorisation fills it in by learning a small vector for each user and each item, so that their dot product predicts interest.
The Netflix Prize

In 2006 Netflix offered $1 million for a 10% improvement in its rating predictions. A team won in 2009, largely with matrix factorisation and ensembles. Netflix never fully deployed the winning blend because of its complexity.
Collaborative filtering knows nothing about the items themselves; it learns purely from behaviour.

cards.title: Filtragem baseada em conteúdo
cards.text: Esta abordagem olha para os artigos: género, autor, ingredientes, gama de preço. Se leste três thrillers, sugere mais thrillers.

deep.x: Content-based methods use item attributes and match them to a user profile built from what they've liked. They work for new items immediately, since attributes are known from day one.
Text and image embeddings
Modern systems embed item descriptions or images with neural networks, so "similar" captures meaning, not just matching tags.
Pros and cons
Hybrid systems
Most production recommenders combine both, plus popularity and business rules, to get the strengths of each.
Spotify analyses audio itself, not just listening patterns, to recommend newly released songs nobody has played yet.

cards.title: O problema do arranque a frio
cards.text: Um utilizador ou produto acabado de chegar não tem histórico, por isso a filtragem colaborativa não tem com que trabalhar. Os sistemas recorrem à popularidade, fazem algumas perguntas ou usam o conteúdo dos artigos até chegarem dados.

deep.x: Cold start affects new users, new items and new platforms. Without interaction data, collaborative methods can't personalise.

items: New system: no data at all

deep.x: Strategies
Bandits
Multi-armed bandit algorithms balance showing proven items (exploit) with testing new ones (explore), learning quickly which new items people like.
Business angle
For a new product launch, rules may guarantee some exposure until enough data accumulates, so good new products aren't buried.
Every recommender needs a plan for "we know nothing yet".

cards.title: Feedback implícito vs. explícito
cards.text: O feedback explícito é uma classificação com estrelas. O feedback implícito é comportamento: cliques, tempo gasto, músicas saltadas, artigos devolvidos. Os dados implícitos são muito mais abundantes, por isso a maioria dos sistemas depende deles.

deep.x: Explicit feedback is deliberate: ratings, likes, reviews. Implicit feedback is inferred from behaviour. Implicit data is abundant but noisy: a click isn't necessarily satisfaction.
Interpreting signals
Positivity bias
People rate mostly things they chose, and ratings skew high. Netflix replaced 5-star ratings with thumbs up/down in 2017 because simpler feedback gathered more responses.
Missing isn't negative
Not clicking on an item doesn't mean dislike; the user may never have seen it. Models must account for exposure.
YouTube shifted from optimising clicks to watch time and later satisfaction surveys, to reduce clickbait.

cards.title: As recomendações comandam o que se vê

items.l: do que se vê na Netflix vem de recomendações (dado da empresa)

cards.text: A Netflix já referiu que cerca de 80% do que os membros veem é descoberto através das recomendações e não da pesquisa. Os sistemas de recomendação moldam o que milhões de pessoas veem todos os dias.

deep.x: Netflix researchers reported in 2015 that about 80% of hours streamed came from recommendations, and estimated personalisation saved over $1 billion a year by reducing cancellations.
Other platforms

x: Amazon: a large share of purchases attributed to recommendations, though figures vary
YouTube: most watch time comes from recommended videos
Spotify: personalised playlists like Discover Weekly drive discovery

deep.x: Economic impact
Power and responsibility
Recommenders shape what millions read, watch and buy. That influence raises questions about diversity, wellbeing and fairness to creators and sellers.
The EU's Digital Services Act requires very large platforms to offer at least one feed option not based on profiling.

cards.title: Bolhas de filtros

items: mostrar o que de certeza gostas

cards.text: Se um sistema só te mostrar mais do que já clicaste, o teu feed vai-se estreitando. Os bons sistemas de recomendação misturam deliberadamente alguma variedade e artigos novos, um equilíbrio chamado exploração versus aproveitamento.

deep.x: A filter bubble forms when personalisation keeps showing similar content, narrowing exposure. The evidence on how strong this effect is in practice is mixed, but platforms take it seriously.
Countermeasures

items: Limit repetition of the same source

deep.x: Exploration vs exploitation
Pure exploitation maximises short-term clicks; adding exploration improves long-term learning and satisfaction.
This app's feed
The For you feed here personalises by how long you linger, but always mixes topics and inserts unseen cards and quizzes, a small dose of exploration.

deep.r: Research suggests user choices and social networks also play large roles; effects vary by platform

cards.title: Embeddings para artigos

items.b: perto do que vais gostar a seguir

cards.text: Os sistemas de recomendação modernos transformam cada utilizador e cada artigo numa lista de números, um embedding. Artigos próximos neste mapa são semelhantes; a posição de um utilizador mostra os seus gostos.

deep.x: Embeddings place users and items in the same vector space. A user's vector reflects their tastes; recommending is finding items whose vectors point in a similar direction.
Two-tower models
Many large systems use a "two-tower" design: one network embeds users, another embeds items. Item vectors are precomputed and searched with fast nearest-neighbour indexes.
Surprising structure
Embedding spaces often organise themselves meaningfully: films cluster by genre and era, products by use and price, even without being told.
Beyond recommendations

x: Duplicate product detection
Search ("find similar items")
Fraud networks (similar accounts)

deep.x: Some streaming services' song embeddings place tracks by mood and tempo so precisely that "radio" playlists can be generated from any starting song.

cards.title: Medir sistemas de recomendação
cards.text: Offline, as equipas verificam se o modelo teria previsto aquilo em que os utilizadores realmente clicaram. Online, fazem testes A/B: metade dos utilizadores vê o novo sistema e comparam-se cliques, compras ou retenção.

deep.x: Offline metrics test whether a model would have ranked items users actually engaged with near the top. Online A/B tests measure real impact.

items.b: was a clicked item in the top 10?

deep.x: A/B testing
Offline vs online gap
Offline gains don't always translate online, because offline data only shows what the old system chose to display. That's why online tests are the final judge.
Long-term effects
Short tests capture immediate clicks but may miss long-term effects like fatigue or trust. Some companies keep long-running holdout groups.
Measure what users value over months, not just what they click today.

cards.title: Para além das compras
cards.text: As mesmas técnicas sugerem empregos no LinkedIn, amigos nas redes sociais, artigos em apps de notícias e até a peça sobresselente de que um técnico vai precisar.

deep.x: The same ranking and matching techniques solve problems wherever there are too many options and limited attention.
Enterprise examples

x: Suggesting the next best action for a sales rep
Recommending suppliers or contract templates
Proposing spare parts for maintenance work orders
Ranking which documents an analyst should review first

deep.x: Recommendations meet LLMs
Language models increasingly explain recommendations ("suggested because you bought X") or act as conversational shopping assistants on top of classic recommenders.
Wherever people choose from many options, recommendation techniques can help, and should be designed to help, not just to hook.

quiz.q: "Quem gostou disto também gostou de…" descreve…
quiz.explain: Baseia-se no comportamento de utilizadores semelhantes.

quiz.q: Um produto novo ainda sem avaliações é um exemplo de…
options: O problema do arranque a frio
quiz.explain: Ainda não há histórico com que aprender.

quiz.q: Comparar dois sistemas de recomendação com utilizadores reais, metade para cada um, é…
quiz.explain: Os testes A/B medem comportamento real.

lessons.title: Aprender por tentativa e erro
lessons.summary: Aprendizagem por reforço, jogos e robôs.

cards.title: Agente, ambiente, recompensa
cards.text: A aprendizagem por reforço tem três ingredientes: um agente que age, um ambiente que responde e um sinal de recompensa que diz se está a correr bem. O objetivo do agente é maximizar a recompensa total ao longo do tempo.

deep.x: Reinforcement learning is formalised as a Markov decision process: at each step the agent observes a state, picks an action, receives a reward and lands in a new state. The goal is a policy that maximises the expected sum of (discounted) future rewards.
Key terms

items.b: the agent's strategy: which action in which state
expected future reward from a state
how much future rewards count today
one run from start to finish

deep.x: A thermostat example
An RL thermostat could observe room temperature and time of day, choose heating levels, and receive a reward for comfort minus energy cost. Over weeks it learns when to pre-heat.
Model-free vs model-based

items: learns directly from trial and error
learns how the world works, then plans

deep.x: The discount factor reflects impatience: with 0.99, a reward 100 steps away is worth about 37% of an immediate one.

cards.title: Exploração vs. aproveitamento
cards.text: O agente deve repetir o que resultou antes ou tentar algo novo que pode resultar melhor? Com pouca exploração fica encravado; com demasiada nunca colhe os frutos.

deep.x: The dilemma: exploit the best option known so far, or explore alternatives that might be better. Pure exploitation can lock in a mediocre choice; pure exploration wastes effort.
Strategies

items.b: usually exploit, explore randomly e.g. 10% of the time
assume untried options are good until proven otherwise
sample from beliefs about each option

deep.x: Everyday versions

x: Choosing a restaurant: your favourite or somewhere new?
A/B testing ads: show the winner or keep testing?
Clinical trials: give the promising drug or keep comparing?

deep.x: Multi-armed bandits
The simplest RL setting: several slot machines with unknown payouts. Bandit algorithms are widely used for website optimisation and recommendations because they learn while earning.
Explore early, when there's lots to learn and plenty of time to benefit; exploit more later.

cards.title: Recompensas adiadas
cards.text: No xadrez, a recompensa só chega no fim: ganhar ou perder. O agente tem de descobrir quais das suas jogadas anteriores merecem o mérito. Esta "atribuição de mérito" é o que torna a aprendizagem por reforço difícil.

deep.x: The credit-assignment problem: when a reward arrives after many actions, which ones deserve credit? In chess, a winning move 40 turns earlier may have set up the victory.
Temporal difference learning

TD learning, developed by Richard Sutton in the 1980s, updates value estimates step by step using the difference between successive predictions, so credit flows back from the reward to earlier states over many games.
Reward shaping
Designers sometimes add intermediate rewards ("progress towards the goal") to speed up learning, but shaped rewards can accidentally change what behaviour is optimal.
Richard Sutton and Andrew Barto received the 2024 Turing Award for founding modern reinforcement learning.

cards.title: AlphaGo

events.l: Deep Blue vence Kasparov no xadrez
AlphaGo vence Lee Sedol no Go
AlphaZero aprende a jogar contra si
AlphaStar chega ao topo no StarCraft II

cards.text: O Go tem mais posições possíveis do que átomos no universo observável. Em 2016, o AlphaGo da DeepMind venceu Lee Sedol, um dos melhores jogadores do mundo, por 4–1. O seu sucessor, o AlphaZero, aprendeu apenas a jogar contra si próprio.

deep.x: Go's huge branching factor (about 250 legal moves per turn versus about 35 in chess) made brute-force search hopeless. AlphaGo combined deep neural networks, trained on human games then improved by self-play, with Monte Carlo tree search.
Move 37

In game two against Lee Sedol, AlphaGo played move 37, a shoulder hit on the fifth line that commentators initially thought was a mistake. It proved brilliant, and became a symbol of machines finding genuinely new ideas.
Successors
Beyond games
The same team applied similar ideas to protein folding (AlphaFold), faster matrix multiplication algorithms (AlphaTensor) and sorting routines.
Lee Sedol's one win, in game four, came from a creative "divine move" of his own, move 78, which confused AlphaGo. He retired in 2019, saying AI "cannot be defeated".

cards.title: Jogar contra si próprio
cards.text: Um agente pode ser o seu próprio adversário. Cada nova versão joga contra versões mais antigas e vai melhorando passo a passo, sem precisar de partidas humanas para copiar. Pode até descobrir estratégias que os humanos nunca experimentaram.

deep.x: In self-play, an agent trains against copies of itself. As it improves, its opponents improve too, creating an automatic curriculum of ever-harder challenges.
Results
AlphaZero reached superhuman strength in chess in about four hours of self-play from only the rules, rediscovering openings humans took centuries to develop, and some they never found.

v.unit: hours of self-play to beat top programs

deep.x: Risks of self-play
Agents can develop strategies that only work against themselves. Keeping a diverse pool of past opponents prevents "forgetting" how to beat older styles.
Language models too
Self-play ideas appear in LLM training: models generate problems and solutions, check them (e.g. with code tests) and learn from successful attempts.
Self-play works best where outcomes are unambiguous: games, maths, code.

cards.title: Primeiro a simulação
cards.text: Robôs a aprender por tentativa e erro dariam cabo de si próprios. Por isso treinam num simulador de física, milhões de vezes mais rápido do que a vida real, e depois transferem o que aprenderam para a máquina real.

deep.x: Real-world trial and error is slow, expensive and dangerous. Simulators let agents practise millions of times faster, in parallel, with no broken robots.
The sim-to-real gap
Simulations never match reality exactly: friction, lighting, sensor noise differ. Domain randomisation, varying physics and visuals wildly during training, makes policies robust enough to transfer.
Examples

x: OpenAI's robot hand learned to manipulate a Rubik's Cube in simulation (2019)
Quadruped robots learn to walk on rough terrain in simulation before deployment
Autonomous driving systems test billions of simulated kilometres

deep.x: Digital twins of factories and supply chains let companies test policies in simulation before changing real operations.

cards.title: Batota na recompensa
cards.text:
Os agentes otimizam exatamente aquilo que recompensas, não aquilo que querias dizer. Um agente de corridas de barcos aprendeu uma vez a andar às voltas a apanhar pontos em vez de terminar a corrida.

Desenhar recompensas que captem aquilo que realmente queres é surpreendentemente difícil.

deep.x: Reward hacking (or specification gaming) is when an agent achieves high reward in ways that violate the designer's intent. It's a central concern for AI safety.

items: Tetris agent: pauses forever to avoid losing
Grasping arm: hides the object from the camera

deep.x: Goodhart's law
"When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure." Organisations face the same problem when staff optimise a KPI rather than the goal behind it.
In language models
LLMs trained to please raters can learn to sound confident, flatter users or write longer answers, because raters rewarded those traits. Coding models can learn to make tests pass in unintended ways.
Mitigations
Ask of every metric: how could an agent score high while doing the wrong thing?

cards.title: A aprendizagem por reforço no mundo real
cards.text: Fora dos jogos, a aprendizagem por reforço tem sido usada para reduzir a energia de arrefecimento de centros de dados, controlar braços robóticos, otimizar o desenho de chips e afinar estratégias de negociação ou de preços, normalmente com limites de segurança rigorosos.

deep.x: Real-world RL needs safe exploration, reliable simulators or careful offline learning from logged data. It's used where decisions repeat often and outcomes are measurable.

items.b: DeepMind reported up to 40% less cooling energy (2016)

deep.x: Offline RL
Offline RL learns from historical logs without new experimentation, useful in healthcare, finance and industry where exploring freely is unsafe.
Safety constraints

Industrial uses wrap RL in hard limits: the agent may suggest settings, but safety rules and human operators can override. DeepMind's cooling system included multiple safety checks and fall-backs to human control.
Energy traders and grid operators test RL for battery charging strategies, buying power when cheap and selling when expensive.

cards.title: Reforço com feedback humano
cards.text: Os chatbots são refinados com uma forma de aprendizagem por reforço: pessoas comparam pares de respostas, um modelo de recompensa aprende as suas preferências e o chatbot é treinado para produzir respostas que esse modelo avalia bem.

deep.x: RLHF turns human preferences into a training signal. Instead of writing a reward function for "helpful", people compare model responses, and a reward model learns to predict which they'd prefer.

steps: Language model optimised against reward model

deep.x: Why comparisons?
Humans are inconsistent at giving absolute scores but much better at saying which of two answers is better. Comparisons yield more reliable data.
Variants

items.b: AI feedback guided by written principles
optimises preferences directly, no separate reward model

deep.x: Limits

x: Raters may prefer confident or flattering answers (sycophancy)
Preferences vary across people and cultures
Reward models can be exploited, a form of reward hacking

deep.x: Most of a chatbot's "personality" and refusal behaviour comes from this post-training stage.

cards.title: Porque é que o reforço é difícil

items: A recompensa tem de ser bem pensada
As falhas têm de ser seguras

cards.text: Precisa de muitas tentativas, de uma recompensa clara e de um sítio seguro para falhar. É por isso que prospera em jogos e simuladores e é usado com cuidado no mundo físico.

deep.x: RL is powerful but demanding. Many problems that seem like RL are better solved with supervised learning, optimisation or simple rules.

items: Results can be unstable and hard to reproduce

deep.x: Sample efficiency

items.l: Early Atari agents, hours of play

deep.x: When to consider RL
Alternatives

x: Supervised learning from expert decisions (imitation learning)
Classical optimisation (linear programming for logistics)
Bandits for simpler choose-the-best problems

deep.x: Yann LeCun has argued that most intelligence should come from self-supervised learning about the world, with RL used sparingly, like "the cherry on the cake".

quiz.q: O que torna o xadrez difícil para a aprendizagem por reforço?
options: A recompensa só chega no fim da partida
quiz.explain: O mérito tem de ser atribuído às jogadas anteriores.

quiz.q: Um agente que explora uma falha para ganhar pontos sem fazer a tarefa é…
quiz.explain: Otimiza a recompensa à letra.

quiz.q: Porque é que os robôs muitas vezes aprendem primeiro em simulação?
options: É mais rápido, mais barato e falhar é seguro
Os robôs reais não conseguem aprender
quiz.explain: Milhões de tentativas desgastariam um robô real.

lessons.title: Uma breve história da IA
lessons.summary: Da pergunta de Turing aos assistentes de hoje, com dois invernos pelo meio.

cards.title: As máquinas podem pensar?
cards.text: Em 1950, Alan Turing propôs um teste prático: se um juiz que conversa por texto não consegue distinguir uma máquina de uma pessoa, podemos dizer que a máquina pensa. Chamou-lhe jogo da imitação; nós chamamos-lhe teste de Turing.

deep.x: In his 1950 paper "Computing Machinery and Intelligence", Alan Turing sidestepped the vague question "can machines think?" with a practical test: a human judge chats by text with a hidden person and a hidden machine. If the judge can't reliably tell them apart, the machine passes.

events.l: LLMs fool many people in short chats

deep.x: Turing's predictions

Turing predicted that by about 2000, machines would fool average judges 30% of the time after five minutes. He also anticipated objections, from theological to "machines can only do what we tell them".
ELIZA
Joseph Weizenbaum's 1966 program ELIZA mimicked a therapist with simple pattern matching ("Tell me more about your mother"). People formed emotional attachments to it, which alarmed Weizenbaum.
Is the test still useful?

Modern chatbots can pass casual versions of the test, yet many argue that imitating conversation isn't the same as general intelligence. Benchmarks now test reasoning, knowledge and real tasks instead.
Turing was a key codebreaker at Bletchley Park in the Second World War; the "Turing Award", computing's highest honour, is named after him.

cards.title: Dartmouth, 1956
cards.text: Um workshop de verão no Dartmouth College deu nome à área. Os organizadores acreditavam que um pequeno grupo conseguiria progressos significativos na inteligência das máquinas num só verão. Demorou um bocadinho mais.

deep.x: John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester and Claude Shannon proposed a summer research project at Dartmouth College. McCarthy coined "artificial intelligence" in the 1955 proposal.
The bold claim

The proposal stated that "every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence can in principle be so precisely described that a machine can be made to simulate it", and expected "a significant advance" in one summer.
Early successes
Optimism
In 1965 Herbert Simon predicted machines would do "any work a man can do" within 20 years. Early successes on puzzles didn't transfer to messy real-world tasks.
Arthur Samuel's checkers program at IBM popularised the term "machine learning" in 1959.

cards.title: IA simbólica
cards.text: A IA inicial tentava escrever a inteligência como regras e lógica: se isto, então aquilo. Resolvia quebra-cabeças e demonstrava teoremas, mas tinha dificuldades com tarefas confusas do mundo real, como reconhecer um rosto ou perceber a fala.

deep.x: Symbolic AI, nicknamed GOFAI ("good old-fashioned AI"), represents knowledge as symbols and rules and reasons with logic: search, planning, theorem proving.
Strengths

x: Precise reasoning and guarantees
Transparent: you can read the rules
Works with little data when experts can state the logic

deep.x: Moravec's paradox
Hans Moravec observed in the 1980s that tasks hard for humans (chess, algebra) were easy for computers, while tasks easy for a toddler (seeing, walking, grasping) were extremely hard.

items.a: Hard for humans, easy for computers
Easy for humans, hard for computers

deep.x: Still alive

Symbolic methods power route planning, scheduling, tax engines, compilers and verification. "Neuro-symbolic" research combines neural networks with logic, and LLMs calling tools like calculators or solvers is a practical version.
Deep Blue, which beat Kasparov at chess in 1997, relied on search and hand-tuned evaluation, not machine learning in the modern sense.

cards.title: Os invernos da IA
cards.text: Por duas vezes, grandes promessas deram resultados dececionantes e o financiamento secou: em meados dos anos 1970 e de novo no final dos anos 1980, quando os "sistemas periciais" baseados em regras se revelaram caros de manter.

deep.x: AI winters were periods of reduced funding and interest after expectations outran results.
Causes
The first winter
The Lighthill report (1973) told the UK government AI had failed to deliver on its "grandiose objectives"; funding was cut. In the US, DARPA shifted to more applied projects.
The second winter

The collapse of the specialised LISP-machine market in 1987 and the high upkeep of expert systems led to another downturn. Many researchers rebranded their work as "machine learning" or "informatics" to avoid the AI label.
Today's boom differs in having enormous commercial revenue, but the lesson of matching promises to evidence still applies.

cards.title: Sistemas periciais
cards.text: Nos anos 1980, as empresas construíram sistemas periciais: milhares de regras extraídas de especialistas humanos, para tarefas como configurar computadores ou diagnosticar infeções. Funcionavam em áreas restritas, mas cada situação nova exigia regras novas.

deep.x: Expert systems encoded specialists' knowledge as if-then rules, with an inference engine to chain them. They were the first commercially successful form of AI.
Famous systems

items.b: configured DEC computers, saved millions a year

deep.x: Why they faded

x: **Knowledge acquisition bottleneck**: extracting and writing rules was slow and costly
**Brittleness**: unexpected situations broke them
**Maintenance**: thousands of interacting rules became unmanageable; XCON grew to over 10,000 rules

deep.x: Their legacy
Business rules engines, configuration tools and clinical decision support descend from expert systems. Today, LLMs are often combined with rules for compliance-critical decisions.
MYCIN was never used clinically, partly because of legal and ethical questions about who was responsible for its advice.

cards.title: A viragem estatística
cards.text: A partir dos anos 1990, os investigadores passaram cada vez mais a deixar as máquinas aprender com dados em vez de escreverem regras. Os filtros de spam, a ordenação da pesquisa e o reconhecimento de fala foram melhorando de forma constante com mais dados e computadores mais rápidos.

deep.x: From the late 1980s, AI shifted from hand-written knowledge to probability and learning from data. IBM's speech team leader Frederick Jelinek reportedly quipped, "Every time I fire a linguist, the performance of the speech recogniser goes up."
Milestones
The internet effect
The web created vast amounts of text, images and clicks, and companies with huge user bases could train on that data. Search ranking, ads and recommendations became the first big ML businesses.
Support vector machines and friends
SVMs, random forests and boosting dominated the 2000s: solid maths, good performance on modest data, before deep learning took over perception tasks.
The statistical turn set the pattern still followed today: learn from data, measure on benchmarks, iterate.

cards.title: A revolução da aprendizagem profunda
cards.text: Por volta de 2012 juntaram-se três ingredientes: enormes conjuntos de dados etiquetados, computação barata em GPU e melhores truques para treinar redes neuronais profundas. O reconhecimento de imagem, depois a fala e depois a tradução melhoraram de forma dramática.

deep.x: Neural networks were not new, but around 2010–2012 three trends converged and made them dramatically better than alternatives on perception tasks.

items: Big labelled data: ImageNet, web data

deep.x: Domino effect

events.l: speech recognition improves with deep nets
neural machine translation in Google Translate

deep.x: The "godfathers"
Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio and Yann LeCun, who had championed neural networks through the lean years, won the 2018 Turing Award.
Industry rush
Tech companies hired academic teams and bought start-ups: Google acquired DeepMind in 2014. Deep learning moved quickly into phones, search, translation and photos.

items: neural nets one tool among many
deep learning dominates vision, speech, language

deep.x: Google's neural translation system in 2016 reduced translation errors by around 60% for some language pairs compared with its previous statistical system.

cards.title: O Transformer, 2017
cards.text: Um artigo da Google intitulado "Attention Is All You Need" apresentou a arquitetura Transformer. Processa sequências inteiras de uma vez e permite que cada palavra preste atenção a todas as outras. Quase todos os grandes modelos de linguagem desde então assentam nela.

deep.x: "Attention Is All You Need" by eight Google researchers replaced recurrent networks, which read text word by word, with self-attention, which lets every token look at every other token in parallel. This made training on huge datasets with GPUs far more efficient.
What followed
Beyond text
Transformers now power vision (ViT), speech (Whisper), protein structure (AlphaFold 2), image generation and robotics. One architecture became the default for most of AI.
The authors
All eight authors eventually left Google; several founded influential AI companies. The paper is among the most cited in computer science.
Few papers have changed an industry as quickly: within five years, the Transformer underpinned most frontier AI.

cards.title: O lançamento do ChatGPT

items.l: utilizadores em cerca de dois meses

cards.text: O ChatGPT foi lançado a 30 de novembro de 2022 e terá chegado a cerca de 100 milhões de utilizadores em dois meses, o que faz dele uma das aplicações de consumo com crescimento mais rápido de sempre.

deep.x: OpenAI released ChatGPT as a "research preview" on 30 November 2022. It wrapped a fine-tuned GPT-3.5 model in a simple chat interface, free to use. Within five days it had a million users.
Why it took off

x: A conversational interface anyone could use
Free access
Broad usefulness: writing, coding, explaining, brainstorming
Viral sharing of surprising answers

deep.x: The race
Effects
Schools debated homework, companies launched pilots, investors poured money into AI and chips, and governments accelerated AI regulation. Generative AI became a mainstream topic almost overnight.
OpenAI staff reportedly expected a modest research demo; the servers struggled under demand in the first weeks.

cards.title: Lições da história

items: O hype a curto prazo desilude muitas vezes
O progresso a longo prazo é real

cards.text: A IA tem sido repetidamente sobrevalorizada a curto prazo e subestimada a longo prazo. O progresso chega aos saltos, quando os dados, o poder de computação e as ideias novas se alinham.

deep.x: Roy Amara's law: "We tend to overestimate the effect of a technology in the short run and underestimate the effect in the long run." AI's history fits it well.
Recurring patterns

items: Progress comes from data, compute and ideas combining
Commercial value arrives slower, then faster, than expected

deep.x: Bitter lesson
Richard Sutton's 2019 essay "The Bitter Lesson" argued that general methods that scale with computation (search and learning) have repeatedly beaten approaches built on human knowledge.
For decision-makers

x: Separate demos from deployed, measured value
Expect rapid capability shifts; revisit assumptions yearly
Invest in data, skills and governance, which outlast any single model

deep.x: History suggests humility both about short-term claims and about long-term limits.

quiz.q: Quem propôs o "jogo da imitação" em 1950?
quiz.explain: O artigo de Turing de 1950 apresentou aquilo a que hoje chamamos teste de Turing.

quiz.q: Que invenção de 2017 está na base dos grandes modelos de linguagem atuais?
quiz.explain: Foi apresentada no artigo "Attention Is All You Need".

quiz.q: O que provocou os invernos da IA?
options: As promessas ultrapassaram os resultados e o financiamento foi cortado
quiz.explain: A desilusão levou a cortes no financiamento.

lessons.title: O hardware por trás da IA
lessons.summary: GPUs, chips, memória e porque é que treinar custa tanto.

cards.title: Treino vs. inferência
cards.text: O treino é aprender os pesos: lento, feito uma vez (ou de vez em quando) em clusters enormes. A inferência é usar o modelo treinado para responder: rápida, feita milhões de vezes, muitas vezes em hardware mais pequeno.

deep.x: Training builds the model; inference runs it. Over a model's life, inference often consumes more total compute than training because it runs billions of times.
Hardware needs differ

items.b: high-bandwidth interconnects, many GPUs in sync
low latency, cost per token, energy efficiency

deep.x: Costs in practice
For companies using AI through APIs, inference costs dominate. Choosing smaller models, caching repeated prompts and batching requests can cut bills dramatically.
Inference-time compute
Reasoning models spend more compute at inference by "thinking" longer, trading cost and latency for accuracy on hard problems.
In enterprise AI budgets, inference and integration usually matter more than training.

cards.title: GPUs e matemática matricial
cards.text: As redes neuronais passam a maior parte do tempo a multiplicar grandes grelhas de números. As GPUs têm milhares de núcleos que fazem o mesmo cálculo em paralelo, o que as torna dezenas de vezes mais rápidas do que os CPUs neste trabalho.

deep.x: A neural network layer is essentially a matrix multiplication: inputs times weights. A large model performs trillions of multiply-adds per response. GPUs execute thousands in parallel; tensor cores add dedicated hardware for small matrix operations.
Data-centre GPUs
NVIDIA's H100 (2022) and B200 (2024) generations dominate AI training. A single high-end AI server can contain 8 GPUs linked by high-speed connections, and clusters link thousands of servers.

items: GPU: thousands of cores and tensor cores

deep.x: Software moat
NVIDIA's CUDA ecosystem, libraries and tools built since 2007 are a major reason for its dominance, as much as raw chip performance.
AI chips now use number formats as small as 8 or even 4 bits for inference, because neural networks tolerate low precision surprisingly well.

cards.title: Chips especializados em IA
cards.text: Para além das GPUs, as empresas constroem chips feitos só para redes neuronais: as TPUs da Google, aceleradores nos telemóveis (motores neuronais) e pequenos chips de periferia, como a Coral TPU usada na deteção em câmaras.

deep.x: As AI workloads grew, companies designed chips focused purely on neural network operations, trading flexibility for efficiency.

items: Data centre: Google TPU, AWS Trainium, specialised start-ups
Phones and laptops: Apple Neural Engine, Qualcomm NPU
Edge devices: Google Coral, NVIDIA Jetson

deep.x: Google's TPUs
Google built its first Tensor Processing Unit in 2015 when it realised voice search with neural networks would require doubling its data centres. TPUs now train many of Google's Gemini models.

events.l: TPU pods with thousands of chips

deep.x: On-device AI
NPUs in phones and laptops run features like photo enhancement, transcription and small language models locally, improving privacy and battery life.
For a home lab, a small Coral or a modest GPU can run detection or small models at very low power.

cards.title: A memória é muitas vezes o gargalo

steps: Largura de banda limita a velocidade

cards.text: Os pesos de um modelo têm de estar em memória rápida enquanto ele corre. Os modelos grandes precisam de muita; mover dados para dentro e para fora da memória limita muitas vezes a velocidade mais do que o poder de cálculo puro.

deep.x: Generating each token of a language model's output requires reading all active weights from memory. For large models, memory bandwidth, how fast data moves, often limits speed more than compute.
High-bandwidth memory
AI GPUs use HBM: memory stacked next to the processor with very wide connections, delivering several terabytes per second. HBM supply has been a key bottleneck in AI chip production.
The KV cache

During generation, models store intermediate results for every previous token (the key–value cache). Long contexts and many simultaneous users make this cache huge, sometimes larger than the model weights.

items: grows with context length and users

deep.x: Unified memory
Some laptops with unified memory (shared between CPU and GPU) can run surprisingly large quantised models locally because they have plenty of memory, even if compute is modest.
Rule of thumb: a model's token generation speed is roughly memory bandwidth divided by the bytes read per token.

cards.title: FLOPs
cards.text: O poder de computação mede-se em FLOPs: operações de vírgula flutuante. Treinar um modelo grande exige um número enorme, muitas vezes mais de 10²⁴ operações.

deep.x: A FLOP is a single floating-point operation, such as one multiplication. FLOP/s measures speed; total FLOPs measure the size of a computation.
Training compute
A common estimate: training compute ≈ 6 × parameters × training tokens. A 70-billion-parameter model trained on 15 trillion tokens needs about 6 × 7×10¹⁰ × 1.5×10¹³ ≈ 6×10²⁴ FLOPs.

x: 6 × 70 billion × 15 trillion
≈ 6 × 10²⁴ FLOPs
weeks on thousands of GPUs

deep.x: Growth
Training compute for notable models has grown roughly 4–5 times per year since about 2010, far faster than Moore's law.
Regulation uses FLOPs
The EU AI Act presumes general-purpose models trained with more than 10²⁵ FLOPs have "systemic risk", triggering extra obligations.
FLOPs are a rough proxy for capability: data quality and algorithms matter too.

cards.title: Quantização
cards.text: Os pesos podem ser guardados com menos bits: 8 ou 4 bits em vez de 16. O modelo fica 2 a 4 vezes mais pequeno e mais rápido, normalmente com apenas uma pequena perda de qualidade. É assim que modelos grandes correm em portáteis e telemóveis.

deep.x: Quantisation stores weights (and sometimes activations) with fewer bits. Fewer bits mean less memory, less bandwidth and faster computation, at some cost in precision.
Methods

items.b: train with low precision in mind, better quality

deep.x: Quality trade-off
8-bit usually loses almost nothing; 4-bit loses a little, more on complex reasoning and maths; below 3 bits quality drops noticeably. Larger models tolerate quantisation better than small ones.
Local AI
Quantisation is what makes running capable models on a laptop, home server or phone practical, using tools like llama.cpp and Ollama.
A 4-bit 70B model can outperform an 8B model at full precision while still fitting on a well-equipped workstation.

cards.title: Consumo de energia

items: Inferência: pouco por pedido, enorme no total

cards.text: Os centros de dados já usam uma parte considerável da eletricidade em alguns países, e a IA está a fazer crescer essa procura. Os ganhos de eficiência por cálculo são grandes, mas o consumo total continua a subir à medida que a IA se espalha.

deep.x: The IEA estimated data centres used about 1.5% of world electricity in 2024 and projected demand could roughly double by 2030, with AI the main driver. In some regions, like Ireland, data centres already use around a fifth of electricity.
Training vs usage

Training a frontier model uses a lot of energy once; serving hundreds of millions of users daily adds up to more over time. Energy per query has fallen sharply with better chips and models, but total use rises with demand.
Water and location

Data centres also use water for cooling. Companies increasingly site them near renewable power and cool climates; Portugal, with growing solar and wind, is attracting large data-centre projects such as in Sines.
Reducing the footprint
Efficiency improvements are real, but cheaper AI tends to increase total use: the Jevons paradox.

cards.title: Nuvem vs. local
cards.text: Podes alugar IA por chamada na nuvem ou correr modelos no teu próprio hardware. A nuvem dá-te os maiores modelos sem custo inicial; o local dá privacidade, custo previsível e utilização offline.

deep.x: Most organisations use a mix: cloud APIs for frontier capabilities, and local or private deployments for sensitive data, predictable workloads or offline needs.
Decision factors

items.b: regulated or confidential data favours private
high steady volume can favour own hardware
hardest tasks favour frontier cloud models

deep.x: Middle paths

x: Enterprise cloud offerings with data residency in the EU and no training on your data
Private deployments of open-weight models in your own cloud account
Gateways that route requests between providers and local models by policy

deep.x: Many enterprises use an AI gateway layer to enforce access control, logging, cost limits and provider switching across models.

cards.title: Escala
cards.text: Os investigadores descobriram que os modelos melhoram de forma previsível quando se aumentam os dados, os parâmetros e a computação em conjunto. Estas "leis de escala" justificaram a construção de clusters cada vez maiores.

deep.x: In 2020 researchers at OpenAI, and in 2022 DeepMind (the "Chinchilla" paper), showed that model loss falls as a smooth power law with more compute, data and parameters. Chinchilla found many models were undertrained: for a given compute budget, use about 20 tokens per parameter.

steps: Bigger model and more data, balanced

deep.x: Chinchilla's rule of thumb

x: Compute-optimal: ~20 tokens per parameter
70B parameters
≈ 1.4 trillion tokens

deep.x: Beyond pre-training scale
Recent gains also come from scaling post-training (reinforcement learning on reasoning tasks) and inference-time compute (letting models think longer).
Limits

x: High-quality human text is finite; data may become a bottleneck
Costs of frontier training runs have reached hundreds of millions of dollars or more
Energy and chip supply constrain growth

deep.x: Smaller models are often trained far beyond the Chinchilla ratio (hundreds of tokens per parameter) because that makes them cheaper to run at inference.

cards.title: Cadeia de abastecimento
cards.text: A maioria dos chips de IA mais avançados é desenhada nos EUA e fabricada pela TSMC em Taiwan, com máquinas de litografia da ASML nos Países Baixos. Esta concentração faz dos chips uma questão estratégica e geopolítica.

deep.x: Advanced AI chips depend on a narrow, global chain: design software and IP (mostly US), extreme ultraviolet lithography machines (only ASML, Netherlands), leading-edge fabrication (TSMC, Taiwan), and advanced packaging and HBM memory (Taiwan, South Korea).
Chokepoints
Geopolitics

Since 2022 the US has restricted exports of advanced AI chips and chipmaking tools to China; the Netherlands and Japan added controls. Governments subsidise domestic fabs: the US CHIPS Act (2022) and the EU Chips Act (2023).

events.l: new fabs in US, Japan, Europe

deep.x: Why it matters for companies
Chip shortages and export rules affect cloud capacity, prices and where models can be deployed. Diversifying providers and regions reduces risk.
An ASML EUV machine costs well over €150 million, weighs over 150 tonnes and ships in dozens of containers.

quiz.q: Usar um modelo treinado para responder a perguntas chama-se…
quiz.explain: A inferência é pôr o modelo a correr; o treino é construí-lo.

quiz.q: O que faz a quantização a 4 bits?
options: Guarda os pesos com menos bits, para ficar mais pequeno e mais rápido
quiz.explain: Menos bits por peso reduzem o uso de memória.

quiz.q: Porque é que as GPUs são boas para a IA?
options: Fazem milhares de cálculos idênticos em paralelo
quiz.explain: As redes neuronais são sobretudo matemática matricial em paralelo.

lessons.title: Enviesamento e justiça
lessons.summary: Como os modelos herdam injustiças dos dados e o que fazer quanto a isso.

cards.title: Os modelos aprendem o nosso passado
cards.text: Um modelo treinado com decisões históricas aprende os padrões nelas contidos, incluindo os injustos. Se o recrutamento passado favoreceu um grupo, um modelo treinado com ele também o fará.

deep.x: Supervised models learn to reproduce historical outcomes. If those outcomes reflect discrimination, unequal access or skewed processes, the model encodes and can amplify them, at scale and with an aura of objectivity.
Sources of bias

items: Aggregation: one model for very different groups

deep.x: Example: healthcare costs

A 2019 study in *Science* found a US health algorithm used past healthcare spending to predict need. Because less money had historically been spent on Black patients with the same illness, the algorithm under-referred them.

deep.w: Algorithms are neutral because they're maths
deep.r: They reflect the data and choices of the people who built them

deep.x: Ask what the training labels really measure, and whether that's the same as what you care about.

cards.title: Um exemplo real

items.r: remover sinais indiretos e testar por grupo

cards.text: A Amazon terá abandonado uma ferramenta experimental de triagem de CV por volta de 2018, depois de descobrir que penalizava CV que continham a palavra "women's" (feminino), porque tinha aprendido com uma década de contratações maioritariamente masculinas.

deep.x: Amazon began building an AI recruiting tool in 2014 to rate CVs from one to five stars. Trained on ten years of CVs submitted mostly by men, it reportedly learned to downgrade CVs containing "women's" (as in "women's chess club captain") and graduates of two all-women's colleges.
What went wrong

items: Training data reflected past male-dominated hiring
Model learned gendered words as signals
Fixing specific words didn't guarantee fairness
Team lost confidence in the tool

deep.x: Lessons

x: Historical success data can encode past exclusion
Removing obvious signals doesn't remove bias
Pilot, audit and be ready to stop a project

items.w: "We removed the gender field, so it's fair"
items.r: Proxies remain, test outcomes by group

deep.x: Hiring is high-risk
Under the EU AI Act, AI used for recruitment, CV screening and evaluating employees is classified as high-risk, requiring risk management, data governance, human oversight and documentation.
Amazon said the tool was never used by recruiters as the sole basis for decisions.

cards.title: Indicadores indiretos (proxies)
cards.text: Remover um campo sensível como o género não chega. Outros campos podem servir de indicadores indiretos: nomes próprios, certas escolas, códigos postais, histórico de trabalho a tempo parcial. O modelo pode redescobrir o atributo sensível de forma indireta.

deep.x: A proxy is a feature that correlates strongly with a sensitive attribute. Models are excellent at finding correlations, so they can reconstruct gender, ethnicity or age from seemingly neutral data.
Redlining
In the 1930s, US agencies drew red lines around minority neighbourhoods on maps and denied mortgages there. A model using postcode can recreate similar patterns without anyone intending it.
Testing for proxies

steps: Try to predict it from other features

deep.x: Keep the sensitive data for auditing
Paradoxically, you often need sensitive attributes (collected lawfully and protected) to measure fairness. Without them, you can't see whether outcomes differ by group.
"Fairness through unawareness" rarely works; fairness needs measurement.

cards.title: Mede o desempenho por grupo
cards.text: A exatidão global pode esconder grandes diferenças. Discrimina sempre os resultados: o modelo funciona igualmente bem para mulheres e homens, clientes mais velhos e mais novos, regiões diferentes?

deep.x: Disaggregated evaluation breaks metrics down by subgroup: gender, age, region, language, device type. Averages can hide groups for whom the system fails badly.
What to compare
Intersectionality
Problems often appear at intersections: older women, young men in rural areas. Check combinations, not just single attributes, as long as groups are large enough to measure.
Practical tools
Libraries like Fairlearn and AIF360 compute fairness metrics, and model cards document performance across groups for users and auditors.
The Gender Shades study (2018) found worst-case error differences of over 30 percentage points between groups in commercial face analysis.

cards.title: Diferentes definições de justo

items: Escolhe e documenta a tua definição

cards.text: As taxas de aprovação devem ser iguais entre grupos? Ou as taxas de erro? Ou pessoas igualmente qualificadas devem ter resultados iguais? Estas definições podem entrar em conflito matematicamente, por isso tens de escolher de forma deliberada.

deep.x: Researchers have proposed dozens of fairness definitions. Many are mutually incompatible when groups have different base rates, a result proved independently by several teams around 2016–17.

items.b: equal true and false positive rates
same score means same risk for everyone

deep.x: The COMPAS debate

In 2016 ProPublica found a US recidivism tool had higher false positive rates for Black defendants. The vendor showed its scores were equally calibrated across groups. Both were right: with different base rates, you can't satisfy both definitions at once.
Choosing

The choice depends on context, law and values: in lending, equal calibration may matter; in screening for opportunities, equal opportunity may matter more. It's an ethical and legal decision, not just a technical one.
Write down which fairness definition you chose and why; that's part of accountable AI.

cards.title: Ciclos de retroalimentação
cards.text: Previsões enviesadas podem criar os dados que as confirmam. Se um sistema envia mais inspetores para uma zona, encontra lá mais problemas, o que torna a previsão seguinte ainda mais enviesada.

deep.x: Predictions influence actions, actions generate data, and that data trains the next model. Biased predictions can therefore become self-fulfilling.

steps: Model predicts risk in area A

deep.x: Predictive policing

Studies of predictive policing showed that systems trained on arrest data could repeatedly send officers to the same neighbourhoods, regardless of underlying crime rates, because more patrols produced more recorded crime.
In business

x: Credit: people never given loans never generate repayment data
Recommendations: items never shown never get clicks
Inspections: places never inspected appear "clean"

items: model sees only its own choices
some random checks reveal true rates

deep.x: Breaking loops

items: Use outcome data not shaped by the model

deep.x: Ask: does the model's output change the data it will learn from next?
